Team —

Saw Sarah's note and HarborTech's attached comments. High-level thoughts from Legal: we should avoid any language that reads like an absolute assignment of IP in model outputs back to the customer. Practical compromise options:

1) Outputs: Offer a customer-focused ownership grant for Outputs generated from their inputs for their internal and commercial use, but exclude assignment of Redwood's pre-existing models and any general model improvements that arise from platform-level telemetry. Proposed phrase: "Customer shall have ownership rights in Outputs generated from Customer Inputs; Redwood retains rights in Platform models and improvements provided such rights do not constitute direct training on Customer Confidential Data without consent."

2) Training / Feedback license: Accept a limited feedback license that permits Redwood to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry and safety-related prompts for model quality and security improvements, but expressly prohibit using identified Customer Input/Output artifacts for retraining without an affirmative opt-in.

3) Telemetry & Audit: Define retention windows for request logs tied to troubleshooting and SLA commitments (e.g., 90 days by default, extendable by order form), and add a reference to audit evidence (SOC2 logs) for enterprise customers.

I'll attach a clean counterproposal for legal to review (redwood_counterproposal_20260830.docx). Laura — please weigh in on privacy/retention specifics. Marcus — quick note on implementation constraints for telemetry redaction would be helpful (latency/cost impact).

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Priyom / Team —

Agree with the proposed compromise language. A couple privacy points to add:

- Retention: Default request log retention = 90 days. For HarborTech enterprise customers we can offer a 12-month option in the order form at additional cost.
- De-identification: Define "de-identified" to mean removal of PII and prompt-level identifiers, and require differential access controls so only aggregated metrics are used for training pipelines.
- Feedback license timing: Training opt-in should be an explicit checkbox on the order form; otherwise assume opt-out for model retraining but allow Redwood to use redacted telemetry for safety/bug fixes.

Marcus — operationally, if we require prompt redaction before storage it will add a small CPU cost to the ingestion path and could increase token latency by ~5-10ms on median. If HarborTech asks for a 12-month retention with separate encryption keys we need a procurement note for dedicated KMS.

If everyone agrees, Legal can push the counterproposal to HarborTech with tracked changes; Jordan — can you request a 30-minute legal-to-legal call this afternoon?

Best,
